messages:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up — we keep hitting subtle streaming warmup failures when customers hotpatch safetensors bundles. Can we sync on canonical header + hotpatch strategy?

anita: saw this in prod yesterday. different exporters reorder metadata and our shard-indexer assumes a stable header order. Streaming loader does wrong byte-range for header+index union.

lee: hmm, are we sure its reorder and not missing optional fields? I thought safetensors had deterministic fields?

anita: fields themselves are stable but many exporters include extra attrs (training_meta, compression_hint) at varied positions. Our simple checksum on header bytes fails.

sam: can we normalize on ingest? compute a canonical header map (sorted keys) and write a canonical sidecar index that's used by runtime. That avoids forcing everyone to change.

jordan: exactly the thought. Proposal: index-first sidecar + canonical header digest. When streaming, loader reads canonical sidecar first (small), validates digest against canonical header, then streams shards. If digest mismatch -> fallback to full header parse.

anita: downside: extra write on ingest (create sidecar). But sidecar is tiny plus we get consistent warmup heuristics and faster failover. Also helps hotpatch diffs (delta apply on canonical index).

lee: question: how does hotpatch work with atomic swap? If we're writing a new bundle and sidecar, how do we ensure no moment of inconsistent header+index visible to loaders?

sam: do an atomic rename on the bundle directory. Steps: write tmp bundle (weights + canonical-sidecar.json), fsync, then rename. Loader treats presence of sidecar+manifest as commit signal.

jordan: +1. Also add a verification step in loader: check canonical-digest in sidecar matches computed digest from streamed header bytes as we pull them. If mismatch, abort stream and fall back to manifest-based full download.

anita: can we avoid double-reading header bytes for digest? That would be extra IO. Maybe include a digest-of-digests: sidecar contains <per-shard-digest> and an index-checksum that loader can verify while streaming shards via range requests (only download small header slices).

lee: we already have per-shard chunk checksums. So sidecar can contain small header summary and per-shard checksums. Loader uses small range GETs to verify headers cheaply.

ci-bot: build 1721 for branch feat/canonical-sidecar failed: integration tests - streaming-loader-retries #41.

sam: ack, looking. Probably a race in the rename logic in test harness.

anita: one more tradeoff: index-first sidecar increases metadata operations to object store (extra GETs). For high QPS cold starts might be sensitive. We should support a fallback fast-path: if request latency budget allows, let loader skip sidecar and stream directly using heuristics, but mark metric 'skipped_sidecar' so Optimize can tune.

jordan: agree. Default: sidecar-first for safety. Tunable policy: allow heuristics-only when tolerable. Capture metrics: sidecar_hit, digest_mismatch, fallback_full.

lee: implementation sketch: \n```\n// sidecar schema (canonical-sidecar.json)\n{\n  \"version\": \"1\",\n  \"canonical_header_digest\": \"sha256:...\",\n  \"shards\": [{\"id\":0, \"offset\": 1234, \"len\": 987654, \"sha256\":\"...\"}, ...]\n}\n```\n
sam: small nit: prefer base64 URL-safe digest for compactness in S3 keys. Also include an optional `delta_patches` array to allow hotpatch application without rewriting whole bundle.

anita: delta patches are great: store patch manifests referencing canonical shard ids. Loader can apply patch by fetching only affected shard ranges. Need clear compatibility rules: patch must target exact canonical_header_digest.

jordan: ok next steps: 1) RFC PR for canonical-sidecar schema + ingestion flow (sam) 2) loader changes: sidecar-first path, digest verification, metrics (lee) 3) test harness: simulate reorder exporters and delta patch apply (anita) 4) integration tests to ensure atomic rename works (ci)

sam: I'll open the PR today. I'll add example exporter shim pseudo-code.

anita: I'll add test vectors (we should include both gzip and uncompressed safetensors).

lee: I'll stub loader changes and add feature flag. We can dogfood on Dedicated first.

jordan: thanks folks. If CI passes, we can roll to staging next week. Also file an ops note about back-compat so infra teams know about rename semantics.

sam: FYI export shim snippet: \n```\n# pseudo\nhdr = read_safetensors_header(input)\ncanonical = {k:hdr[k] for k in sorted(hdr.keys())}\nsidecar = {\"canonical_header_digest\": sha256(json.dumps(canonical)), ...}\nwrite(tmp_bundle, weights)\nwrite(tmp_bundle + \".sidecar\", json.dumps(sidecar))\nfsync(tmp_bundle, tmp_bundle + \".sidecar\")\nrename(tmp_bundle -> bundle)\n```\n
anita: great. I'll post test failures and sample broken bundles in #eng-ml later. :+1:

lee: thanks. Closing thread for now — reopen if we hit more reorders.
